answers.children: Norwich Terriers are moderately good with children. Their compact 9-10 inch build and feisty yet affectionate nature suit respectful older kids who match the breed's boundless energy, but their determined terrier spirit can lead to overly enthusiastic play that overwhelms toddlers. The small size allows them to dart around small spaces without knocking things over, while their loyal bond with family encourages gentle interaction when boundaries are clear.
answers.other-pets: Norwich Terriers do not always get along with other pets. Their high prey drive, inherited from ratting and fox hunting roots, makes them likely to chase or harass small animals, while their stubborn streak can create tension with same-sex dogs. The feisty temperament means early introductions are essential, as these pint-sized hunters retain the instinct to pursue vermin despite their affectionate side with family.
answers.exercise: Norwich Terriers need 45-60 minutes of exercise daily. Bred for ratting and bolting foxes from dens, they thrive on walks combined with games that tap their hunting drive such as fetch or scent work, yet without it their boundless energy leads to digging or destructive chewing indoors. The compact build supports agile activity in small yards, matching their determined spirit.
answers.shedding: Norwich Terriers shed lightly year-round. Their medium wire coat lacks the dense undercoat of many breeds, so loose hairs are minimal and do not cling heavily to furniture, though the wiry texture still requires regular hand-stripping to maintain its characteristic crisp feel. The coat's moderate length suits their small 10-12 lb frame without creating heavy seasonal blowouts.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic, yet the Norwich Terrier is sometimes suggested for allergy sufferers because its medium wire coat sheds lightly and produces less loose dander than softer-coated small breeds. The wiry texture that developed for farm ratting traps hair close to the body rather than releasing it freely into the home environment.
answers.training: Norwich Terriers are moderately easy to train. Their intelligence of 7 supports quick learning, but the stubborn streak from their independent ratting heritage makes them resistant to repetitive commands, demanding consistent motivation that channels their determined and feisty nature rather than relying on blind biddability.
answers.lifespan: Norwich Terriers live 12-15 years. Their small 10-12 lb build and robust health contribute to this range, while the compact proportions developed for squeezing into fox dens and farm spaces support an active life that sustains vitality well into later years without excess strain on joints.
answers.size: Norwich Terriers reach 10-12 lb and stand 9-10 in tall. The sturdy yet compact build, honed for ratting and bolting foxes, feels surprisingly solid for its diminutive height, allowing the feisty terrier to navigate tight spaces while remaining easy to lift and carry in small homes.
answers.barking: Norwich Terriers bark moderately. Their alert vocalisations, rooted in the need to signal vermin during East Anglian hunts, tend to target strangers, cats or outdoor movements rather than sounding constantly, with the feisty temperament producing sharp but brief bursts that match their 6 barking score.
answers.apartment: Norwich Terriers can live in apartments. Their compact size and adaptability of 7 allow them to settle indoors after exercise, though their moderate barking at passers-by and high energy require daily outings and puzzle toys to prevent the destructive habits that emerge when their hunting drive lacks outlet.
answers.first-time: Norwich Terriers are not ideal as a first dog. Their stubborn streak during training and high prey drive demand an owner who can channel the feisty, determined terrier nature without being overwhelmed by the independent spirit that once made them effective at squeezing into fox dens unaided.
